header.title: Component Architecture
header.description: Explore Front-end Design Patterns, Atomic Design, and Performance Optimizations.

atomic.title: Atomic Design
atomic.description: A methodology for creating design systems by breaking them down into five distinct levels.

whatIs.title: What is Atomic Design?
whatIs.content: Atomic Design is a methodology composed of five distinct stages working together to create interface design systems in a more deliberate and hierarchical manner.

atoms.label: Atoms:
atoms.description: The basic building blocks of matter (e.g., Buttons, Inputs, Labels).

molecules.label: Molecules:
molecules.description: Groups of atoms bonded together to be the smallest fundamental units of the compound (e.g., Search Form combining Input and Button).

organisms.label: Organisms:
organisms.description: Groups of molecules joined together to form a relatively complex, distinct section of an interface (e.g., Header).

templates.label: Templates:
templates.description: Page-level objects that place components into a layout and articulate the design's underlying content structure.

pages.label: Pages:
pages.description: Specific instances of templates that show what a UI looks like with real representative content in place.

visualizer.controlsDescription: Change Atoms to update the entire UI.

container.title: Container vs Presentational
container.description: A pattern for separating business logic/data fetching from UI rendering.

presentational.label: Presentational Components:
presentational.item2: Receive data and callbacks via props.
presentational.item3: Rarely have their own state (except for UI state).

container.label: Container Components:
container.item2: Provide data and behavior to presentational or other container components.
container.item3: Often stateful, serving as data sources.

evolutionWithHooks.title: Evolution with Hooks
evolutionWithHooks.content: In modern React, this pattern involves Custom Hooks. Instead of wrapping a component in a Container, we can extract the business logic into a hook (e.g., useDogImages) and use it directly within the component. This achieves the same separation of concerns with less nesting.

visualizer.summary: The Container (left) handles how things work (fetching data, state), while the Presentational (right) handles how things look (rendering HTML/CSS). This separation makes components more reusable and easier to test.

patterns.title: Component Architecture Patterns
patterns.description: Advanced patterns for component composition and reusability.

compoundComponents.title: Compound Components
compoundComponents.description: Components that work together to form a complete UI, often sharing state implicitly (e.g., via Context API). Users can arrange the sub-components flexibly.

renderProps.title: Render Props
renderProps.description: A technique for sharing code between React components using a prop whose value is a function.

hoc.title: Higher-Order Components (HOC)
hoc.description: A function that takes a component and returns a new component, typically to inject props or logic. Popular in the past (e.g., Redux connect), but often replaced by Hooks today to avoid "Wrapper Hell".

compound.heading: Implicit State Sharing
compound.characteristic: Sub-components (Tab, TabPanel) communicate via Context provided by parent (Tabs), not via direct prop passing from user.

renderProps.heading: Logic Reuse via Function Prop
renderProps.characteristic: The component doesn't decide what to render, but delegates that decision to the render prop function, sharing its internal state (x, y).

hoc.heading: Logic Injection (Wrapper)
hoc.characteristic: A function that takes a component and returns a new component ("Wrapper"), injecting new props or behavior (like the Spinner).

performance.title: Performance Patterns
performance.description: Techniques to optimize rendering and application performance.

memoization.title: Memoization
memoization.description: Caching the result of an expensive function call and returning the cached result when the inputs occur again.
memoization.reactMemo: HOC to skip re-rendering a component if its props haven't changed.
memoization.useMemo: Hook to memoize a computed value.
memoization.useCallback: Hook to memoize a callback function definition.

virtualization.title: Virtualization (Windowing)
virtualization.description: Rendering only the items in a list that are currently visible (plus a small buffer) instead of the entire list. This significantly improves performance for large datasets. Libraries like react-window or react-virtualized are commonly used.

visualizer.nonMemoized: I re-render every time parent updates!
visualizer.memoized: I only render when MY props change.
visualizer.flashNote: *Colored backgrounds flash on render. Notice red side flashes on every button click.
visualizer.virtualOn: Currently rendering only visible items + buffer. Fast!
visualizer.virtualOff: Rendering ALL 1000 items. Check the DOM node count!
